title: Structure Across Voices: Comparing acoustic-event type accumulation and sequence dependence across four vocal repertoires using frozen audio encoders
abstract: arXiv:2609.16612v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vocal repertoires can differ in acoustic-event type accumulation and temporal organization, yet direct comparison is difficult because corpora use different native events and unequal amounts of sequence. We compare sperm whale codas, human speech phones, Bengalese finch syllables, and common marmoset calls using the same frozen-audio-encoder procedure while matching event count and local sequence opportunity. Whale shows the fastest type accumulation; Finch shows the strongest immediate dependence and repeated-subsequence recurrence. Physically interpretable acoustics recover complementary parts of this profile, continuous analyses without clustering support broad Whale acoustic coverage, and source- and position-preserving nulls retain both Finch order effects. translated_title: 跨声音的结构：使用冻结音频编码器比较四种发声曲库中的声学事件类型累积与序列依赖性
translated_abstract: 发声曲库在声学事件类型累积和时间组织方面可能存在差异，但由于语料库使用不同的原生事件且序列数据量不均等，直接比较十分困难。我们在匹配事件数量和局部序列机会的条件下，使用相同的冻结音频编码器程序比较了抹香鲸的尾声、人类语音音素、孟加拉雀的音节和普通狨猴的叫声。鲸类表现出最快的事件类型累积；雀类表现出最强的即时依赖性和重复子序列复现。具有物理可解释性的声学特征能够恢复该特征图谱的互补部分，无需聚类的连续分析支持了鲸类广泛的声学覆盖范围，且保留来源和位置信息的零假设检验保留了雀类的两种顺序效应。扩展预测上下文使比较结果向鲸类倾斜。因此，曲库差异取决于所测量的声学属性和时间尺度，而非形成一个简单的排序。
tldr: 本研究利用统一的冻结音频编码器方法跨物种比较四种发声系统，发现不同物种的发声结构优势取决于所测量的声学属性和时间尺度，而非简单的优劣排序。
en_tdlr: This study uses a unified frozen-audio-encoder approach to compare four vocal systems across species, revealing that repertoire differences depend on the acoustic property and temporal scale measured rather than forming a simple ranking.
